name: Melbourne
description: Central Melbourne from open data, from Docklands to the Shrine, lit by the real sun. Every shadow is computed, and every height is traceable to its source.

imagery.attribution: No open aerial imagery covers central Melbourne, so the ground is drawn from Overture Maps land use, land, water and transport (OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL)

water.note: The Yarra and Victoria Harbour; the GA DEM flattens the river to 0 m.

waves.note: A light northerly across a river 100-150 m wide: short-fetch ripples. Chosen values, not a measurement.

water.colour_note: The Yarra is turbid with suspended clay, brown-green with well under a metre of visibility.

protection.title: Melbourne Planning Scheme, DDO10 and clause 15.01-1L-03
protection.summary: A permit must not be granted for buildings and works that cast any additional shadow on these public spaces in their protected hours (DDO10, Table 1).
protection.source_note: Read from the live Melbourne Planning Scheme (version VC314, 28 October 2026) through the Victorian government's planning API: DDO10 section 2.3, Tables 1 and 2, and clause 15.01-1L-03. Table 2 spaces get a discretionary test (no unreasonable prejudice to their amenity), so they show sun but are not tested. The State Library forecourt and the Shrine of Remembrance's northern forecourt are in Table 1 but are not mapped as named spaces in the open data. The Royal Botanic Gardens (DDO15) and Fitzroy Gardens (DDO13, DDO20, DDO21) windows were not checked against the scheme text.
protection.reading_note: Every DDO10 window falls between 22 April and 22 September, outside daylight saving, so clock time and standard time agree. The 22 March windows for the Royal Botanic Gardens and Fitzroy Gardens fall in daylight saving; which time they mean is not settled here. Baseline: the scheme compares against the buildings standing when a permit is decided, while this test compares against today's model.
protection.tip: Tip: try a site just north of Federation Square, or west of City Square.

reference_heights.source: Wikipedia, List of tallest buildings in Melbourne (revision 1382111188, 26 October 2026)

tour.title: Central Melbourne from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings from OpenStreetMap via Overture Maps, standing on Geoscience Australia's 5 m LiDAR terrain. No openly licensed aerial photo covers the city, so the ground is drawn from the open map data: parks, plazas, streets, laneways and tram tracks.

tour.title: Federation Square, 22 June
tour.text: Melbourne's planning scheme forbids any new shadow on Federation Square from 11 am to 3 pm between 22 April and 22 September. At midwinter the sun stands only 29° above the northern horizon at noon.

tour.title: Southbank's towers
tour.text: Australia 108 (317 m) and Eureka Tower (297 m), both mapped in OpenStreetMap to within a metre of their published heights. Their winter shadows fall south, away from the river.

tour.title: The Hoddle Grid at noon
tour.text: Robert Hoddle's 1837 grid is turned about 20° from the compass: Collins, Bourke and Lonsdale Streets run at a bearing of 70°. The Bourke Street Mall is protected from noon to 2 pm on 22 April and 22 September.

tour.title: The Arts Centre spire
tour.text: 162 m of lattice above the Theatres Building, rebuilt taller in 1996. OpenStreetMap maps it as a thin block; here it is a parametric model, lit at night.

sources.planning: Melbourne Planning Scheme via api.app.planning.vic.gov.au (VC314, 28 October 2026)

game.title: Melbourne on Foot
game.blurb: Walk central Melbourne rebuilt from open data and lit by the real sun. Talk to the people who know it, take the river shuttle down the Yarra, and fly past the Arts Centre spire. Every fact they tell you comes from the model.

climate.source: Bureau of Meteorology, Melbourne (Olympic Park) 086338, mean maximum temperature since 2013

game.ferry_note: Wharves and the helipad are from OpenStreetMap via Overture. Melbourne has no regular ferry through the city, only river cruises and the Port Phillip Ferries from Docklands, so this river shuttle and its vessel names are invented. Victoria Harbour meets the Yarra just west of the model, so the shuttle stops short of Docklands. Routes are generated through the river, and boats run at 1.5 times a cruise boat's speed. At a wharf you can skip the wait.

links.name: St Kilda and Brighton
links.how: Route 96 runs from the city to St Kilda, where the little penguins come ashore after dark.

ferry_style.note: An invented river shuttle, smaller than a harbour ferry.

npcs.name: Mia
idle: Federation Square is protected from new shadow from 11 to 3, every day from 22 April to 22 September. You can test a tower against that rule in the 3D model.
Route 96 runs from the city to St Kilda. After dark the little penguins come ashore on the breakwater there: open St Kilda and Brighton from the menu (Esc).

npcs.name: Hannah

npcs.name: Arjun

npcs.name: Sophie

lines.title: Report back
lines.on_open: All three surveys done. Report back to Mia at Federation Square.

quests.title: Welcome to Fed Square
talk: You're the new surveyor? Good. This city is rebuilt from open data: {buildings} buildings on Geoscience Australia's LiDAR terrain, under the real sun.
There's no open aerial photo of Melbourne, so the ground you're standing on is drawn from the map data: streets, laneways, parks and tram tracks.

There are three surveys to do, in any order. The square: Hannah, in City Square up Swanston Street, on the planning rule for sun. The river: Arjun runs the shuttle from Federation Wharf, and Sophie flies from across the water. The heights: Jun, in Birrarung Marr.
WASD or the arrow keys to move, Shift to sprint, X to walk, drag to look around. E to talk, and T to switch between surveys.

choices.text: The square: Hannah, in City Square
The river: Arjun, at Federation Wharf
The heights: Jun, in Birrarung Marr

quests.title: Winter sun
talk: Melbourne's planning scheme lists the spaces no new building may shade. Federation Square is protected from 11 am to 3 pm, every day from 22 April to 22 September.
On 22 June at 12:30, {sun:Federation Square|6-22|12:30}% of the square gets direct sun. The sun is only 29° up at noon in midwinter.
Go back down to Federation Square and find a sunny spot at lunchtime on 22 June. The sun meter under the map ray-casts from where you stand.

steps.text: Stand in direct sun on Federation Square, 11:00 to 15:00 on 22 June

quests.title: Down the Yarra
talk: The planning scheme protects the river too: no new shadow across the Yarra corridor from 11 to 2 on 22 June.
Take the shuttle downriver to Crown Landing. Sophie keeps the helicopter at the city helipad, just across the water.

steps.text: Take the river shuttle from Federation Wharf to Crown Landing
Meet Sophie at the Melbourne City Helipad

quests.title: Over the spire
talk: Ready? The Arts Centre spire is 162 m of steel lattice. In OpenStreetMap it's a thin block; here it's built from its published height.
Fly upriver past the spire and set down in Birrarung Marr.
Space to climb, C to descend, W and S for forward and back, A and D to turn. V switches to a bird's-eye view. E gets you out once you've landed.

quests.title: Where heights come from
talk: Every building here carries the source of its height. {share:mapped}% of the footprint area has a surveyed height and {share:floors}% a floor count; the rest is estimated.
Aim at a building and press Q to use the survey lens. Find one with a surveyed height, one from a floor count and one that's estimated.

steps.text: Survey lens (Q): a surveyed, a floor-count and an estimated height

quests.title: Survey complete
talk: That's the full tour: the square, the river, the air and the data underneath it all.
{acc:matched} towers have been checked against their published heights, with a median error of {acc:median_abs_error_pct}%. Now you know where the other numbers come from.
The city is yours. Change the time of day, take the shuttle, or fly anywhere.
